subject: Computer Networking
title: APIs: Machines Talking to Machines
description: A micro-lesson that makes APIs: Machines Talking to Machines usable.

hook.text: A weather app on your phone doesn't have its own satellites. It asks another server for the forecast via an API.

buildup.text: An API defines the endpoints, parameters, and responses a server offers. It's a contract between systems.

discovery.text: REST APIs use HTTP verbs and URLs. GET /users/42 fetches user 42. Clean, predictable, widely adopted.

twist.text: APIs power almost everything: payments (Stripe), maps (Google), auth (OAuth). Apps are just API glue.

climax.text: When an API changes without warning, apps break. That's why versioning and documentation matter.

punchline.text: APIs let apps borrow each other's superpowers.

quiz.question: What is an API in the context of the web?
options: A defined interface that lets programs communicate with each other
A visual design tool for websites

details.summary: APIs allow software applications to communicate with each other programmatically. Web APIs use HTTP to let clients request data or actions from servers. REST APIs dominate the web, returning structured data like JSON instead of HTML pages. APIs enable mobile apps, integrations, and microservices.
details.whyItMatters: APIs power the modern internet. Mobile apps, third-party integrations, and microservices all communicate through APIs. They are the backbone of software interoperability.
takeaways: APIs let applications communicate programmatically via HTTP
REST APIs return structured data like JSON instead of HTML
APIs enable mobile apps, integrations, and microservices

faq.question: What makes an API RESTful?
faq.answer: REST APIs use standard HTTP methods: GET to read, POST to create, PUT to update, DELETE to remove. They are stateless, with each request containing all needed information. Resources are identified by URLs. REST is a set of principles, not a strict specification.

faq.question: Why are APIs important for mobile apps?
faq.answer: Mobile apps cannot render server-side HTML like browsers. They need raw data to display in their native interfaces. APIs provide structured data that mobile apps can parse and present. The same API can serve web apps, mobile apps, and third-party integrations simultaneously.
